correctness.rationale: All 0/1 partial matching incidence points are polytope vertices by bipartite total unimodularity. The classical adjacency theorem reduces degree to one connected alternating path or cycle. Four exhaustive and disjoint types have counts alpha_k, \(pq\)*(1+alpha_k), (p+q)*alpha_k, beta_k. The recurrence alpha_{k+1}=(k+1)(alpha_k+1) yields the stated difference, proven positive by all k,p,q cases except the enumerated 2-by-2 and simplex equality. Exact-integer brute checks on 1,011 vertices and 820 parameter pairs independently corroborate, but are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is the complete rectangular two-parameter rank-degree multiset and sharp monotonicity/exception classification, not the known alternating path/cycle criterion. General prior good-component counting and the inclusion-monotonicity theorem (Abreu et al. 2019) and Merino–Mütze traversal (2023) do not explicitly provide this evaluation or its inequalities in inspected portions. Similar square-matrix face work (Cao–Chen 2022) remains an identified full-text access risk; priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Cao–Chen (2022) full text was inaccessible; although its abstract concerns one-dimensional faces, it may already encode or explicitly state the square-case rank-degree formula.
Alternative rook-monoid/partial permutation matrix terminology could conceal an equivalent earlier numerical degree theorem; search nonappearance is not novelty proof.
The older general matching-good-path degree theorem provides the starting framework; a reader may consider the new enumeration a specialization rather than a deep conceptual advance.

value.rationale: The degree multiset is a natural invariant of a 0/1-polytope skeleton. The formula and multiplicities determine every rank stratum for all positive rectangular dimensions, exact total edge count, strictness/equality classification refining the published weak monotonicity theorem, without generating the exponentially many matchings. This is a natural complete classification with direct polyhedral content, not a one-off lookup or repetition of the general adjacency criterion.
